regenerable_on: any guest running systemd whose system bus the capture user can reach, with busctl on PATH. Two shapes have to be there or most of this variant is a listing of targets and sockets: something must be RUNNING CONTAINERS, because the docker scope is where ContainerID and the transient-unit-file path come from, and the guest must carry units that reference names it does not have, which an upgraded distribution does by itself — the 41 not-found units here are what an Ubuntu image accumulates across releases, not something anybody staged. A freshly installed minimal guest regenerates a payload with neither. Every figure below is this host's own unit table, so a re-stage moves the object count and the referrer lists with it, and the anchors are re-read by hand in the same change or they are asserting a machine that is gone.
anonymisation_note: Scrubbed against harness/scrub/units.json, and this is the variant that found the escaping gap. systemd writes ONE identifier three ways inside a single ListUnits row — a partition UUID appears plain in the device unit's Description (/dev/disk/by-uuid/<uuid>), `\x2d`-escaped in the unit NAME derived from that path, and escaped a second time as `_5cx2d` in the D-Bus object path derived from the name — and the free-text pass reads a leaf as written, so two of the three were invisible to it. Measured before anything was changed: 54 strings carried an identifier only a fold reveals, and the independent detectors reported ZERO findings on the unscrubbed capture, so nothing in the publish gate could see the channel. The two encoding formats (unit_name, object_path) fold before they substitute and restore the escaping afterwards; all three spellings of one identifier now come back as one replacement, which is what keeps the specimen internally consistent as well as scrubbed. 30 substitutions: 20 partition and filesystem UUIDs, 7 ZFS partlabel ids, the pool's own u64 guid — 18 digits, which the free-text pass's 19-digit floor also missed — the pool name and the login user's name. The detectors were run over the committed bytes afterwards and report nothing.
note:
735 units off one Ubuntu 26.04 guest's system bus: 299 devices, 230 services, 70 targets, 51 sockets, 34 mounts, 20 timers, 12 slices, 11 scopes, 6 paths and 2 automounts. The payloads are four request/response maps rather than four documents, because this interface has no single document to be — a collection here is 2 manager calls, one Properties.GetAll per unit systemd could not load (41), and one Properties.Get per service and scope (241) — and every key IS the busctl argument line that produced the reply beside it, so a reader checks a value by pasting the key after `busctl call org.freedesktop.systemd1 ` and adding `--json=short`.

What this variant exists to teach is the backwards walk. 41 of these units are names systemd LISTED and could not load, and the finding belongs to the units doing the referencing, not to the absent name — which has no fragment, no owner and nothing to change. So the walk runs from the absent end (one GetAll each) and lands the facts on the referrer: 41 units here carry MissingOrdering, three carry MissingWants, and NONE carries MissingRequirements, which is the measurement DESIGN 20's own note predicts (zero hard references on every host measured) rather than a gap in the capture. The absent names get the other half of the same walk: 41 ReferencedBy lists saying who asked for them, which is the only thing such a row can say.

Stated bounds, because a specimen shows one machine on one day.

MissingRequirements is declared, implemented and reached by NOTHING here, so the hard-dependency arm of the rulebook — the one that says a start job fails before the unit runs — is exercised by no committed pair. MissingReferenceUnobservable is likewise unreached: it stands for a probe that could not run or a listing too large to probe in full, and this host's 41 absent units are far below the 200 the adapter probes and every GetAll answered. MachineName is unreached too — libvirt was installed on this guest and no domain was running, so no machine-qemu scope existed to derive a domain name from, and the runs-to-domain relationship that only that fact can mint is minted by nothing.

The row carries values only. No names family, no absent list, no unobservable record, no relation assertion — the acquisition path publishes none of those four channels, so the commit's assertions and unobservable counts are structurally zero rather than incidentally so.

Eight docker scopes carry ContainerID, and the id is published verbatim: harness/scrub/docker.json already rules that a docker id is minted from randomness and denotes nothing outside the daemon that minted it, and the units and docker collections join on that same value, so substituting it here alone would delete the join the two specimens exist to demonstrate.

And one shape here is a REPORTED DEFECT of the reference rather than a reading of the machine: `home.mount` and `sysroot.mount` are not-found units that also carry RuntimeSynthesised true, because the adapter's fileless-mount test asks only whether the name is in ListUnitFiles and a name systemd could not load is in no file list by construction. The glossary sentence for that fact says systemd made the unit up from the mount table, which is false for a name systemd could not load at all. The pair reproduces it because agreement is the bar; it is the reference's to answer for.
anchors_note:
Read off the four payload files by hand at staging, before any stream existed, which is what makes them an authority the reference-generated half is not. Seven assert a value and three assert an absence.

commit_objects 735 is the length of the array in listunits.json's one reply, counted. It is anchored because absence is not the only way to lose a collection: a port that dropped the not-found units as uninteresting, or that emitted the cgroup tree twice by walking it and then appending the tail, satisfies every fact anchor below and reports a different number here.

Slice `system.slice` on ssh.service is the only anchor that comes from the per-unit Properties.Get, and it is what makes that 241-call arm non-optional: a port that skipped it reproduces every other anchor. It is read from unit-slice.json's reply for ssh.service's object path.

ContainerID `5b3e81546f70` is the first twelve characters of the 64 in the scope's own name, and nothing else on the row says it — the Description is dockerd's `libcontainer container <the same 64>`, which names nothing an operator recognises. Anchored against the docker collection's spelling of the same value, because that shared value IS the join.

RuntimeSynthesised true on run-docker-netns-1492676d77f2.mount is the ListUnitFiles cross-check, and it is a claim about TWO documents: the name is in the listing and is in no unit file. A port that never read the second document publishes no such fact.

MissingOrdering on docker.service and ReferencedBy on firewalld.service are the two ends of ONE edge, anchored separately on purpose. docker.service's file says After=firewalld.service and this host has no firewalld; the fact lands on docker.service, which has a file and an owner, and firewalld.service's row says who asked for it. A port that walked forwards from every unit would have to make 735 property reads to find the first, and one that published the finding on the absent name would satisfy the second and fail the first.

MissingWants on apport-autoreport.service is the soft class, and it is anchored beside that same unit's absent MissingRequirements because the two are the distinction the adapter refuses to flatten: a Wants= systemd cannot resolve is documented as ignored, a Requires= is a start job that fails, and this row carries the first and not the second. Note that apport-autoreport.service carries MissingOrdering as well — whoopsie.path appears under both After= and Wants= — so the anchor also proves the two directives land in different facts rather than being merged by name.

The two absent Slice anchors are different claims and neither implies the other. NetworkManager.service is a not-found SERVICE: the Get was made for it, systemd answered with the empty string, and an empty read is not a slice membership — a port that published `Slice: ""` fails here. dev-disk-by\x2ddesignator-esp.device is a DEVICE: it is not in the cgroup tree at all, so no Get is made for it and the payload holds no reply to read — a port that asked for every unit's Slice would find no captured request and could only invent one.

Deliberately not anchored: the tree ORDER. The systemctl-status walk is what acquire() spends its ordering on, and the stream carries no depth member and the judge compares records by identity rather than by position (DESIGN 19: order inside a stream is not significant), so an anchor on it would be asserting something no consumer of this stream can see.
